newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve was expected to add reserves to the banking system via a round of overnight system repurchase agreements (RPs) on Wednesday, economists said.

Wednesday marked the end of the current two-week maintenance period and federal funds opened under pressure, last trading at 5.63 percent, above the Fed's current official target level of 5.50 percent.

"The Fed has in place $20.45 billion in three-, nine- and 14-day fixed RPs. Our estimates indicate that this total should cover the technical add need for the day," said Marc Wanshel, economist at Morgan Guaranty Trust Co.

However, the Fed has been consistent in aggressively adding reserves on settlement days, regardless of the technicals, Wanshel said. He said the Fed most likely would intervene with a modest round of overnight system RPs. But another possibility was that it would attempt to get a head start in replacing the three- and nine-day RPs that mature on Thursday.
In that case, it could opt for an eight-day operation of about $10 billion, Wanshel said.
